::: {.poster-left}

## Motivation

Academic posters are among the most common formats for sharing
research, yet most fail basic graphic design principles — even
award-winning posters are structured like journal articles rather
than visual communication (Faulkes, 2023). Worse, they are
distributed as PDFs: fixed-size files that require zooming on
screens, are inaccessible to screen readers, and cannot reflow
to different display contexts.

## The Better Poster Concept

Morrison (2019) proposed a three-column landscape layout with the
main finding in the centre, methods on the left, and figures on
the right. Empirical evidence supports this: Bentsen & Østergaard
(2026) found significant advantages for the Better Poster format
in first impression ($p = 1.64 \times 10^{-6}$) across 103 posters
at a real scientific conference.

## Methods

Betterland is a Quarto extension with five components:

1. **`_extension.yml`** — format declaration, disables Bootstrap
2. **`template.html`** — semantic HTML5 skeleton (`<header>`, `<main>`, `<aside>`)
3. **`poster.lua`** — ~230 line Lua filter, populates five template slots
4. **`poster.css`** — CSS Grid (`1fr 3fr 1fr`), fluid `clamp()` typography,
   responsive reflow below 1024px
5. **`poster-print.css`** — A0 typography and `@page { size: A0 landscape }`

## Key Design Decisions

- **Full methods retained** in left column — informed by Oronje et al. (2024),
  who found billboard-poster viewers wanted more methodological detail
- **Semantic HTML5** throughout — following WCAG 2.2 (W3C, 2023),
  making output more accessible than PDF by default
- **Breakpoint at 1024px** — boundary between tablet landscape
  (three-column viable) and portrait (not viable)

## Authoring Experience

The entire poster is written in Markdown and YAML — no HTML or CSS
required. Content goes into two named zones:

```markdown
::: {.poster-left}
## Methods
## Results
:::

::: {.poster-right}
## Figures
## References
:::
```

:::

::: {.poster-extras}
*Additional content goes here if really necessary (figures).*
:::

::: {.poster-right}

## Feature Comparison

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 5.2
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| out-width: "100%"

tools = ['PowerPoint', 'beamerposter', 'posterdown', 'betterposter',
         'docposter', 'acad-poster', 'Betterland']

features = {
    'Morrison layout':      [0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1],
    'Web/screen first':     [0, 0, 0, 0, 0.5, 1, 1],
    'Responsive design':    [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1],
    'Literate programming': [0, 0.5, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1],
    'Multi-language':       [0, 0, 0, 0, 0.5, 0, 1],
    'QR auto-generation':   [0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1],
    'Semantic HTML5':       [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0.5, 1],
    'A0 print support':     [1, 1, 1, 1, 0.5, 0, 1],
    'Quarto native':        [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1],
    'Open source':          [0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
}
feature_names = list(features.keys())
scores = [sum(features[f][i] for f in feature_names)
          for i in range(len(tools))]
colors = ['#cccccc'] * 6 + ['#0b4545']

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.2, 3.8))
bars = ax.barh(tools, scores, color=colors, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)
ax.set_xlabel('Features supported (out of 10)', fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlim(0, 10.5)
ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax.set_title('Feature coverage by tool', fontsize=9,
             fontweight='bold', pad=6)
for bar, score in zip(bars, scores):
    ax.text(score + 0.1, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2,
            f'{score:.0f}' if score == int(score) else f'{score:.1f}',
            va='center', fontsize=7, color='#333333')
highlight = mpatches.Patch(color='#0b4545', label='Betterland (this work)')
ax.legend(handles=[highlight], fontsize=7, loc='lower right', framealpha=0.7)
plt.tight_layout(pad=0.5)
```

## Responsive Layout

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 5.2
#| fig-height: 2.4
#| out-width: "100%"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.2, 2.4))
ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
ax.axis('off')
ranges = [
    (0.0,  0.30, '< 1024px\nMobile / tablet portrait',
     'Single column\nheader → finding\n→ left → right', '#e8f4f8'),
    (0.33, 0.63, '1024–1279px\nLaptop',
     'Three columns\nPage scrolls if\ncontent is dense', '#fff3cd'),
    (0.66, 0.96, '≥ 1280px\nLarge monitor',
     'Three columns\nFits viewport\nNo scroll needed', '#d4edda'),
]
for x0, x1, label_top, label_bot, color in ranges:
    rect = mpatches.FancyBboxPatch(
        (x0 + 0.02, 0.10), (x1 - x0 - 0.04), 0.80,
        boxstyle="round,pad=0.01",
        facecolor=color, edgecolor='#aaaaaa', linewidth=0.8)
    ax.add_patch(rect)
    ax.text((x0 + x1)/2, 0.80, label_top, ha='center', va='center',
            fontsize=7, fontweight='bold', color='#333333')
    ax.text((x0 + x1)/2, 0.38, label_bot, ha='center', va='center',
            fontsize=6.5, color='#555555', linespacing=1.4)
ax.set_title('Responsive layout breakpoints', fontsize=9,
             fontweight='bold', pad=4)
plt.tight_layout(pad=0.3)
```
